summary: Coimbra is a dense Euro where each round you draft dice that double as currency, action-strength, and a track-advancement resource, forcing constant trade-offs about what to give up. It rewards building engines across several interlocking tracks (ships, coins, monastery favors) that all pay off at game end.
praised: tight interlocking economy with real trade-offs
criticised: steep rules overhead and analysis paralysis
bidding/dice-drafting can feel fiddly to teach
some randomness in dice rolls frustrates planners
can run long for a mid-weight game

interaction.detail: Players draft dice in turn order and can be blocked from taking the die or advisor they wanted, and the shared player-order track and artisan/ship spaces create competition for limited slots. Most of the actual building happens on each player's own tableau and tracks, so it's parallel development with periodic friction points.

subsystems: card-effect VP engine (four color decks: nobility, clergy, merchants, explorers)
sources: victory point track advanced by played cards
scoring.how_you_win: You draft dice each round to buy cards and take actions, most of which push your marker up a shared VP track immediately, then add a final round of card-driven bonuses; after the fixed number of rounds the highest total wins.
